alt: Counting the ranges of consecutive days that contain at least one outage, a reading of 0, by counting the opposite. Each day, run is the number of ranges ending that day that contain no zero, and clean adds them up. The answer is the total number of ranges minus clean.

steps.caption: Day 0 reads 3, so `run` becomes 1: 1 range ends on day 0 without containing an outage. `clean` grows to 1.
Day 1 reads 0, an outage, so `run` resets to 0: no range ending on day 1 is clean. `clean` stays 1.
Day 2 reads 5, so `run` becomes 1: 1 range ends on day 2 without containing an outage. `clean` grows to 2.
Day 3 reads 2, so `run` becomes 2: 2 ranges end on day 3 without containing an outage. `clean` grows to 4.
Day 4 reads 0, an outage, so `run` resets to 0: no range ending on day 4 is clean. `clean` stays 4.
Day 5 reads 0, an outage, so `run` resets to 0: no range ending on day 5 is clean. `clean` stays 4.
Day 6 reads 4, so `run` becomes 1: 1 range ends on day 6 without containing an outage. `clean` grows to 5.
Day 7 reads 1, so `run` becomes 2: 2 ranges end on day 7 without containing an outage. `clean` grows to 7.
All 8 days are read. There are 8 * 9 / 2 = 36 ranges in all and 7 of them are clean, so 36 - 7 = 29 ranges contain at least one outage.
